Given the current interest rate environment and market conditions, a laddered maturity structure with the following allocations could provide a stable return and minimize duration risk:

We can allocate 7% of the portfolio to a 5-year Treasury bond (0.35 in the 5-year bucket), 6.5% to a 10-year Treasury bond (0.32 in the 10-year bucket), and 2% to a 2-year Treasury bill (0.1 in the 2-year bucket). This balance will not only meet the 10-year duration requirement but also provide a decent yield, while ensuring the laddered maturity structure guideline is followed.

This allocation maintains the current maximum single maturity exposure within the 2.5% threshold (6.5% in the 10-year bucket). It's also below our warned duration limit of 7 years.
